title: The Long Climb in JGB Yields Is Nearly Over
standfirst: JGB yields saw a historic rise between 2022 and 2026. Most of the rise came from higher inflation expectations and a normalization of term premia. Our analysis shows the Long Climb is likely nearly over.
_note: Titles, source notes and y-axis labels are the TITLE / SOURCE / YLABEL constants of each chart script in the JMA chart library, copied verbatim. Windows, chart form and series labels are read off the same scripts' plotting code — the data CSV cannot carry them.

charts.title: A 4% yield is a first for many in Japan
charts.source: Source: MOF daily par-yield curve, JMA
charts.note: The 20Y, then the longest JGB, last closed above 4% in May 1995. The 40Y, now the longest, regained 4% on 18 May 2026 — a 31-year absence, closed and then given up again.

charts.title: Long-run rate i* rose by 100bp since 2021
charts.source: Source: BoJ Review 2026-J-5 six-model r* ensemble (JMA weighting), BoJ-CIE extended, JMA JGB yield-curve model. Year-end; 2026 as of July.
charts.note: Both components are baselined at zero rather than stacked, so a negative r* points down — the bar tops do not sum to i*, which is why the line carries the sum explicitly. Faded bars are provisional: r* is measured only through December 2024. The underlying data is monthly; the chart samples year-end, which is what the article's figures quote.
